label: D1 of last ~10 trials: ramps with episode trial, boosted after S1 and no reward, shaped by value
terms: (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * value ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * (ep_trial - 90) ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * (ep_trial - 90) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * (ep_trial - 90) * value ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_dec == 9) * value**2
explanation: Fires only at D1 in the last episode decile (trials 90-99); essentially zero at GO and D2 and earlier in the episode (timing alone R^2 0.28). Within that window the magnitude ramps up with ep_trial, and the ramp is steeper when the previous trial reached S1 (after a2 S1 r/u and a1 S1 u it is highest, after S2 lowest). It is also higher after an unrewarded previous trial. The model value output shapes it: a positive main effect with a concave value**2 term, and a negative value x ep_trial interaction, so late-episode D1 steps with low value grow fastest. All terms are observed or model-internal; none are future. Six terms reach dev R^2 beyond timing 0.81 and test 0.80, well above the profile additive all ceiling of 0.05, because that ceiling has no within-decile ep_trial ramp. Remaining error: the largest activations (about 2.5-3) are underpredicted.

issues: The 'explained' verdict holds up. On test, the six terms score 0.800 R^2 beyond timing (total R^2 0.857 vs timing-only 0.284). Misses shows no systematic gap: mean error by phase is about 0, and the largest (phase, previous-trial) cell errors are around ±0.016. No term uses a future variable.

The ramp is understated. The growth within the last ten trials happens almost entirely after an S1 trial, not just more steeply after S1. A plain ramp scores only 0.079 (0.082 with prev_reward added). Ramp x (prev_state==1) lifts this to 0.484, and its weight is +0.152 while the unconditioned ramp turns slightly negative (-0.027). Separate ramps give +0.125 after S1 and -0.031 after S2. In the agent's fit the base ramp only looks positive because it is offset by the ramp x value term.

The claim 'higher when the previous trial was unrewarded' is weak and depends on what else is in the fit. On its own with the ramp, the prev_reward==0 weight is negative (-0.024). It only turns positive (+0.14 to +0.22) once value is in the model, and it adds just 0.007 R^2 (0.793 to 0.800) on top of S1-ramp + S1-ramp x value + value.

The value effect also sits mainly on the S1 ramp. With S1-ramp x value in the fit, a general ramp x value term gets weight about 0.003. Three terms (S1 ramp, S1 ramp x value, value) already reach 0.793 test. So 'low value grows fastest' really means 'after S1, low value grows fastest'.

What is left over is the shape of the ramp: it saturates. Adding ramp^2 x S1 (plus value^2 terms) raises test R^2 to 0.843. This is consistent with the agent's note that the largest activations are under-predicted. There is a small amount of firing in decile 8 (e.g. 1.19 at trial 88), but a decile-8 S1-ramp term gets weight about 0.
